[P5] 出版者的话

古希腊圣哲亚里士多德曾说：“任何人都会生气，这没什么难的，但若要适时适所地以适当方式对适当对象恰如其分地生气，可就难上加难了。”我们现在讲的情绪管理指的就是要适时适所地对适当对象恰如其分地表达情绪。

现实生活中，人们越来越多地认识到情绪管理能力的重要性，因为这方面能力出众的人往往在各个领域都游刃有余；相反，此项能力差的人，虽然可能很聪明，但做起事来往往很吃力。

情绪管理能力虽部分得益于先天因素，但归根结底还得靠后天的学习和培养。幼儿时期是情绪管理能力培养的黄金时期，一个人在幼儿时期所获得的情绪经验和习惯会在大脑中形成永久的神经联结，对其身心发展影响很长远。

当前，亲子共读情绪管理类图画书这种情绪管理能力培养方式已被广泛认可。优质的图画书好比幸福的种子，通过父母的声音飞进孩子的耳朵里，植根在孩子的心底，施以阳光、雨露就能生根、发芽。

这套有趣的动物图画故事书温情脉脉，每一本都是有针对性地就孩子的某一种情绪话题展开，描绘孩子的心路历程，揭示其走出情绪困扰并解决问题的过程。每一本书都附有幼教专家精心撰写的导读，可作为家长亲子共读时的参考。

让我们在这套书的陪伴下，去享受一段美妙的亲子阅读之旅吧

[P6] 老师对你说
出发吧，小蜗牛
有一只名叫贝林戈的小蜗牛，特别爱学习。爱学习让他拥有了一个从杏子到罗马花椰菜无所不知的聪明脑子。
想不想听听他的冒险经历呢？实际上，那是在猝不及防的情况下发生的。他在生菜叶上散步的时候，生菜被人带到了菜市场。就这样，连他也一起被带走了。在城市，他偶遇了大狗莫列顿，和他成为了好朋友，并帮助他解决了难题。为了表示感谢，莫列顿带他参观城市。他们逛遍了城市的大街小巷，大开眼界。最后，莫列顿把小蜗牛安然无恙地送回了家。
故事以小蜗牛的微观视角呈现，充满着新奇和趣味感。看着看着，我们就会明白，这不正是孩子们眼中的世界吗？他们对未知的世界永远充满着好奇心和探索欲。小蜗牛之所以能够了解城市，归根结底是因为他心底深处有一个去城市里大开眼界的念头。而聪明的小蜗牛也的的确确赢得了朋友的信任，开拓了眼界，心灵得到了成长。
反观当下教育现状，有些不尽如人意的情况。身边不乏这样的家长：把所有他们觉得危险的因素都事先帮孩子“屏蔽”掉，给孩子规定许多的禁区，让孩子在一个没有风雨的“温室”中生活。结果呢，导致很多孩子在上了小学后，还不敢一个人出去买东西，因为大人一直不允许他们

[P7] 外出；不会做饭，因为大人禁止他们接触带火和带电的东西；不会削苹果，因为大人害怕刀会划伤他们的手……

可是，很多事情早晚要孩子独立去完成，更何况有些是孩子平时很难见到的，或者从来没有想过的事情。我们应该鼓励孩子去发现和探索，而不是关在“温室”里，让孩子享受不到阳光的滋润和风雨的吹打。教育家蒙台梭利说过：“听过的会忘记，看过的会记得，做过的才会理解。”只有让孩子亲身经历了世界的错综复杂，体验了其中的苦辣酸甜，才能内化为自己的经验，才能有勇气在将来的世界中，突破藩篱，大胆挑战。

作为家长，一定要鼓励孩子在已有的知识储备的前提下，亲身去探索和了解世界。这样，等到有一天孩子的羽翼渐渐丰满时，我们就可以放心地让孩子飞出去，并告诉孩子：世界很大很精彩，自己去看看吧！

（保定市教科所教研员 刘育红）

[P14] 当他正准备咬一口面前这个巨大的“猕猴桃”的时候，“猕猴桃”突然动了一下。
贝林戈简直不敢相信自己的眼睛——这不是个“猕猴桃”！
在他面前的是一只开始吼叫的大狗，而那个“猕猴桃”竟然是大狗毛茸茸的脸！
“你为什么大叫啊？”贝林戈问道，“我还没有伤到你呢！”，
“哦……你是没伤到我，可是我有点儿怕你。”大狗弱弱地回答道。

[P16] “我叫莫列顿，我有大大的牙齿！”为了吓唬小蜗牛，大狗继续说道。
“我呢，我才没有牙齿呢！”贝林戈保证说。
“那么，你会叮人吗？”莫列顿问道。
“我才不会呢！我是一只蜗牛，我十分柔软的！”贝林戈自豪地回答。
莫列顿解释说，他有一次遇到过一只小虫子，被叮了一下。
从那以后，他的一只爪子就一直肿着。

[P18] “别担心，我能给你治好！”贝林戈拍着胸脯说道。
原来，灰胡子爷爷曾经教过贝林戈如何治疗昆虫叮咬。
小蜗牛挠挠脑袋，把头侧到一边，然后又侧到另一边，晃来晃去，真思考着。

[P5] Publisher's Note

The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle once said: 'Everyone gets angry, and that's not difficult. But to be angry at the right time, in the right place, with the right person, and in the right way—well, that's much harder.' What we now call emotional management is precisely about expressing emotions appropriately, at the right time, in the right place, and toward the right person.

In real life, people are increasingly recognizing the importance of emotional management skills. Those who excel in this area often thrive in various fields; conversely, those who lack this ability, though perhaps intelligent, often struggle in their endeavors.

While emotional management skills may partially stem from innate factors, they ultimately rely on learning and cultivation over time. Early childhood is the golden period for developing emotional management skills. The emotional experiences and habits formed during this time create lasting neural connections in the brain, profoundly influencing a child's physical and mental development.

Currently, the practice of parent-child reading of emotional management picture books is widely recognized as an effective way to cultivate emotional intelligence. High-quality picture books are like seeds of happiness, carried into children's ears by parents' voices, taking root in their hearts, and growing with sunlight and rain.

This series of heartwarming animal picture storybooks focuses on specific emotional topics for children, illustrating their inner journeys and revealing how they overcome emotional challenges and solve problems. Each book includes a carefully written guide by early childhood education experts, serving as a valuable reference for parents during shared reading.

Let us enjoy a wonderful parent-child reading journey together with this series.

[P6] Teacher Says to You
Let's Go, Little Snail
There is a little snail named Belingo who loves learning. Loving to learn gave him a smart brain that knows everything from apricots to Roman cauliflower.
Want to hear about his adventure? Actually, it happened unexpectedly. While he was strolling on a lettuce leaf, the lettuce was taken to the market. That way, he was taken along too. In the city, he met a big dog named Morleton, became good friends with him, and helped him solve a problem. To show his thanks, Morleton took him on a tour of the city. They wandered through the city's streets and alleys, broadening their horizons. Finally, Morleton safely returned the little snail home.
The story is presented from the snail's microscopic perspective, full of novelty and fun. As we watch, we'll understand—this is exactly the world as children see it! They are always full of curiosity and a desire to explore the unknown. The reason the little snail was able to understand the city is because deep down, he had a strong desire to broaden his horizons in the city. And indeed, the clever little snail earned his friend's trust, broadened his horizons, and grew emotionally.
Looking at today's education, there are some unsatisfactory situations. There are not a few parents like this: they shield their children from all the dangers they perceive, set many restrictions, and let their children live in a 'greenhouse' without storms. As a result, many children, even after starting elementary school, still dare not go out alone to buy things, because adults have never allowed them to.
Welcome to follow Songta Beibei, free to share
The growth treasure trove of playful and explorative Songta Beibei

[P7] Going out; unable to cook, because adults forbid them from touching things with fire or electricity; unable to peel apples, because adults fear knives might cut their hands...

However, many things will eventually need to be done independently by children, especially those they rarely see or have never even thought about. We should encourage children to discover and explore, rather than keeping them in a 'greenhouse' where they cannot experience the nourishment of sunlight or the challenges of wind and rain. As educator Montessori said: 'What is heard is forgotten, what is seen is remembered, what is done is understood.' Only by personally experiencing the complexity of the world and tasting its bitterness, spiciness, sourness, and sweetness can children internalize these experiences and gain the courage to break through barriers and face challenges in the future.

As parents, we must encourage children, based on their existing knowledge, to personally explore and understand the world. This way, when their wings are gradually fully grown one day, we can confidently let them fly out and tell them: The world is vast and wonderful—go see it for yourselves!

(Researcher, Baoding Education Research Institute, Liu Yuhong)

He felt that being called that made him seem like a poor little creature without a brain.
In fact, his aunt in Burgundy always told him to enrich his mind.

[P1] 本页为绘本封面，标题为《小蜗牛什么都不怕》，展示了主角小蜗牛手持地图、背着糖果壳，站在城市街道上，背景有房屋、骑车的小男孩和黄色小狗，整体氛围活泼可爱。
[P2] 本页为绘本版权页，展示了作者、译者、出版社等信息，背景插图延续封面风格，呈现小蜗牛在城市街道中的场景，旁边有骑车的小男孩和黄色小狗。
[P3] 本页为绘本的扉页，展示了书名《小蜗牛什么都不怕》、作者、译者、出版社等信息，并配有主角小蜗牛的插图，背景简洁，突出书籍主题。
[P4] 本页为绘本的版权信息页，详细列出了图书在版编目（CIP）数据、作者、译者、出版社、出版时间、ISBN、定价等信息，以及版权和印刷信息。
[P5] 本页为出版者的话，阐述了情绪管理的重要性，强调幼儿时期是培养情绪管理能力的关键期，并介绍了该系列图画书通过亲子共读帮助孩子管理情绪的理念和价值。
[P6] 本页为绘本的导读页，以‘老师对你说’为标题，介绍了主角小蜗牛贝林戈的冒险故事梗概，包括他因生菜被带到菜市场、在城市结识大狗莫列顿并一同游览、最终安全回家的经历，并延伸讨论了儿童探索欲与现代教育中过度保护的问题。
[P7] 本页为一位教育工作者撰写的导读或推荐语，强调应鼓励孩子独立探索世界，而非过度保护，引用蒙台梭利的教育理念，呼吁家长放手让孩子体验生活，以培养其勇气和独立性。
[P8] 本页介绍了主角小蜗牛贝林戈因被称作‘我的小豌豆’而感到不悦，强调他其实拥有丰富的知识。页面配有多彩蔬菜插图，包括大葱、洋葱、豌豆、芜菁、罗马花椰菜、西红柿、胡萝卜、茄子、洋蓟和芦笋，并附有二维码及推广语。
[P9] 画面中，小蜗牛贝林戈坐在一个巨大的南瓜上，正在阅读《果蔬大百科》，周围环绕着苹果、西葫芦、萝卜、柿子椒、橙子等蔬菜水果，旁边还有其他书籍和放大镜，右下角有二维码及推广语，整体展现其热爱学习、探索果蔬知识的形象。
[P10] 小蜗牛贝林戈在生菜上散步时，被一只戴着黄色手套的手提起来，掉进了一个装满蔬菜的篮子里，他惊慌地想喊救命。画面展示了这一惊险瞬间，右下角有推广二维码。
[P11] 小蜗牛被关进一辆装满蔬菜的卡车里，感到非常担忧，思考如何逃出去。画面展示了一辆黄色的果蔬卡车，车身上写着“瓜果蔬菜”和“马塞尔果蔬店”，司机正在驾驶，车顶有三只小鸟。
[P12] 小蜗牛贝林戈被带到一个热闹的菜市场，他好奇地观察四周，并因看到许多食物而感到兴奋，决定尝试一个从未吃过的毛茸茸水果。
[P13] 小蜗牛贝林戈来到一个热闹的菜市场摊位前，摊位上摆满了南瓜、西红柿、蘑菇、卷心菜等新鲜蔬果，他好奇地观察着周围，右下角有推广二维码。
[P14] 小蜗牛贝林戈误把一只大狗的脸当成猕猴桃准备咬，大狗因此惊叫，贝林戈询问原因，大狗表示自己只是有点害怕。
